newsitem.title: UK: Almost two-thirds of Britons say no to EMU - poll.
newsitem.headline: Almost two-thirds of Britons say no to EMU - poll.

text.p: Almost two-thirds of Britons would vote against participation in a single European curency if a referendum were held now, according to a MORI poll on Wednesday commissioned by The European newspaper. Both main political parties have promised to hold a referendum should they decide to sign up to EMU.
In addition, 58 percent of the 1,025 polled said Britain's future in Europe should not be decided along party political lines, but by a free vote in the House of Commons.
Three out of four people surveyed favoured a 48-hour maximum working week and around half mistrusted the French as an EU ally.

The poll also showed the younger population was more in favour of the European Union than older generations and two thirds of the sample said they believed the next generation will feel more European.
